# PeerVault

> PeerVault sends a file straight from one browser to another with end-to-end encryption, so it never lands on a server you have to pay for or trust.

PeerVault transfers files directly browser-to-browser without server storage. Files are chunked into 64 KB blocks, each encrypted with AES-256-GCM using the Web Crypto API. A lightweight Go relay server handles WebRTC signaling only — it never sees file data. PeerVault is in pre-release and is not published to npm.

## Status

- Pre-release (v2.0.0, no npm publish, no production adopters)
- License: AGPL-3.0-or-later (see LICENSE)
- Tests: 67 passing (`cd sdk && npm test`)

## Cryptography — what the code actually implements

PeerVault performs a hybrid post-quantum handshake by default.

- **ML-KEM-768 (FIPS 203)** is implemented from scratch in Rust under `pqc/`: polynomial ring `Z_q[X]/(X^256+1)` with `q=3329`, NTT/inverse NTT, CBD sampling, FIPS 203 encoding/compression, and implicit rejection. It compiles to a 49 KB wasm module with no imports and no allocator, embedded in the SDK as base64.
- **Validation:** all 100 NIST KAT vectors pass key generation, deterministic encapsulation, decapsulation, and implicit rejection. `sdk/tests/hybrid.test.mjs` cross-checks decapsulation against Node/OpenSSL's independent ML-KEM-768 implementation and runs a 200 KB end-to-end transfer over in-memory WebRTC.
- **Handshake:** the receiver sends an ephemeral ML-KEM-768 public key, an ephemeral P-256 public key, and a nonce, all HMAC-SHA256-authenticated with the share-link key. The sender encapsulates to both and returns the KEM ciphertext, its P-256 key, and a key confirmation. Both sides derive `session = HKDF(ECDH || ML-KEM)` and `file_key = HKDF(share_link_key || session)`.
- **Share-link key:** a random 256-bit key in the URL fragment. Browsers never send fragments to servers. It authenticates the handshake and is mixed into the file key, so a signaling relay cannot substitute keys.
- **Chunks:** AES-256-GCM with a fresh 96-bit IV per 64 KB chunk. The entire 21-byte frame header `[type:1][fileIndex:4][chunkIndex:4][IV:12]` is authenticated as AAD.
- **Capabilities:** `PQCrypto.isMLKEMSupported()` reports whether the bundled wasm core can run. `CryptoEngine.getCapabilities().usesPostQuantumKeyExchange` becomes true only after a completed handshake.
- **Opt-out:** `hybridHandshake: false` on both peers falls back to the share-link key for compatibility with pre-PQC builds; that path is classical and not post-quantum.

## Real exported symbols

Verified from `sdk/dist/index.mjs`:

- `PeerVaultSender` — manages file selection, WebRTC setup, chunking, encryption, and sending
- `PeerVaultReceiver` — manages joining the room, decrypting chunks, and file assembly
- `PQCrypto` — classical ECDH/HKDF primitives plus `hybridKeyExchange()`; `isMLKEMSupported()` reports whether the bundled ML-KEM wasm can run.
- `MlKem768` / `HybridHandshake` — the FIPS 203 wasm API and the authenticated ML-KEM-768 + P-256 handshake.
- `CryptoEngine` — AES-256-GCM chunk encryption/decryption and key generation/import
- `FileChunker` / `FileAssembler` / `CHUNK_SIZE` — the chunking and reassembly path
- `PeerConnection` / `SignalingClient` / `DEFAULT_ICE_SERVERS` — transport internals, exported so a TURN server can be supplied

## Installation (working paths only)

- jsDelivr CDN: `https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/itsoumya-d/peervault@main/sdk/dist/index.mjs`
- Clone and build: `git clone https://github.com/itsoumya-d/peervault && cd peervault/sdk && npm install && npm run build`

## Integration recipe

```javascript
import { MlKem768, HybridHandshake, CryptoEngine } from
  'https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/itsoumya-d/peervault@main/sdk/dist/index.mjs';

// ML-KEM-768 primitives (backed by the bundled FIPS 203 wasm)
const kem = await MlKem768.load();
const keyPair = kem.generateKeyPair();
const { ciphertext, sharedSecret } = kem.encapsulate(keyPair.publicKey);
const opened = kem.decapsulate(ciphertext, keyPair.secretKey);
// opened.valid === true && opened.sharedSecret equals sharedSecret

// The default sender/receiver path runs HybridHandshake automatically.
// Both peers must share the same 32-byte share-link key.
const alice = await HybridHandshake.create('sender', shareKey);
const bob = await HybridHandshake.create('receiver', shareKey);
const finish = await alice.acceptHello(await bob.createHello());
const ready = await bob.acceptFinish(finish);
await alice.acceptReady(ready);
```

Full browser-side sender/receiver usage requires a live WebSocket relay and RTCPeerConnection.

## Known limitations

- No TURN relay by default: connections fail behind symmetric or carrier-grade NAT. The default ICE configuration uses three public STUN servers (`stun.l.google.com:19302` x2, `stun.cloudflare.com:3478`) and no TURN server. Pass `{ iceServers: [...] }` to `PeerVaultSender`/`PeerVaultReceiver` to add TURN. A failed ICE negotiation now emits a distinct `error` naming the ICE state, and `connect()` rejects rather than hanging.
- Transfers are not resumable. If either tab closes, the transfer restarts from the beginning.
- The receiver assembles files in memory by default (`Blob`); opt into `sinkFactory` with `createFileSystemSink()` to stream to disk. Large files otherwise remain bounded by device RAM.
- Post-quantum cryptography is implemented (ML-KEM-768 wasm + P-256 hybrid) but has not been independently audited. `hybridHandshake: false` falls back to the classical share-link-key path.
- File reconstruction is entirely in browser RAM — large files (multi-GB) may exhaust device memory.
- 1:1 only: the relay supports one sender and one receiver per room.
- No npm publication: CDN or git clone only.
